      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Tier-1 member owning bounded work: steps, context construction and fit, acquisition, activation, evaluation, derived-surface staleness, result refinements, disposition, totality, refinement and licensing, work state and restart, cost and proportionality, and closed-result reuse. It uses, without redefining, the objects and core result algebra of FOUNDATIONS and the frame object and activate outcomes of REFERENCE_FRAME.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":25,"quote":"core for admission, activation and steps (§3); it redefines nothing those\nmembers own. A route","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION","start_line":24}],
      "key": "activation_member",
      "label": "ACTIVATION"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Activation of one reference frame or one declared active frame configuration on an exact subject. Its context is the activated frame's projection to the actor, never the corpus or workspace. Intake, admission, applicability and activation remain distinct even within one invocation.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":37,"quote":"A step is the activation of one reference frame, or one declared active\nframe configuration, on an exact subject (REFERENCE_FRAME §1, §11). Its\ncontext is the projection of that activated frame to the actor; the corpus\nor the workspace is never the context (P0; RF-002). Intake, admission,\napplicability and activation are distinct relations inside the step even\nwhen one invocation performs all of them.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step","start_line":32}],
      "key": "step",
      "label": "Step"
    },
    {
      "conditions": ["Instance premises are selected outcome and acceptance conditions; work that may exceed one activation; actors with declared capability envelopes; and an admitted grant. Individual consequences use the premise subsets stated in the source table."],
      "definition": "Foundation-to-law family for transitions, steps and configuration, covering sections 1 and 4. These instance premises condition its governed work, are not commitments, and do not follow from finite capacity alone. The table identifies P0 as recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 as independent; P4b as derived from P0 and P2 with the non-reacquirability premise; and P5 as derived from P0 and P6 with the open-world premise.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":58,"quote":"Foundation to law. This family, transitions, steps and configuration,\ncovers this section and §4. Its instance premises are: (a) a selected\noutcome with its acceptance conditions; (b) work that may exceed one\nactivation's capacity; (c) actors with declared capability envelopes; (d)\nan admitted grant. They are conditions of the work this family governs,\nnot commitments, and do not follow from finite capacity alone. The\nstanding of the consequences below is stated in\n[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law).","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step","start_line":51}],
      "key": "transition_law_family",
      "label": "Transitions, steps and configuration foundation family"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Material workspace state and authoritative inputs together with justifiable knowledge and explicit unknowns. Work state records workspace, governing basis, still-applicable closed results and judgments, residuals and external-effect uncertainty. An actor's context is an account of this state, not the state.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":125,"quote":"The work state of §5 records it:\nthe workspace, the governing basis, and the closed results and judgments\nthat still apply, with the residuals and the uncertainty over external\neffects as the explicit unknowns. An actor's context is an account of the\ncurrent state, not the state itself\n([§5](#the-workspace-and-an-actors-account)) (P3, P5).","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step%2FTransitions","start_line":120}],
      "key": "current_state",
      "label": "Current state A"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Owner-defined constraint predicate comprising the selected outcome, its acceptance conditions and governing obligations. It admits multiple realised states rather than naming one state. In construction it is Z, supplied by the selected WHAT across the owning Product's Intent, Product and Specification; their descriptions refine Z.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":131,"quote":"The destination is defined by constraints: the selected outcome with its\nacceptance conditions (Outcome U, [FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology))\nand the governing obligations the work must keep. It names no single\nstate: its acceptance conditions admit several realised states. Its\nowning authority defines it (P2, P6).","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step%2FTransitions","start_line":127},{"end_line":219,"quote":"The\ngoverning specification, the selected WHAT across the Intent, Product and\nSpecification of the Product that owns the work, supplies Z; its\ndescriptions refine Z.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step%2FConstruction%20relation","start_line":216}],
      "key": "destination",
      "label": "Destination Z"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Bounded change from current state to next state carried out by one step. Work fitting one activation is a single transition; larger work is refined into a series, each with its own step and applicable outer obligations.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":140,"quote":"A transition is a bounded change from the current state to a next state,\ncarried out by one step. Where the work exceeds one activation's capacity,\nthe outer transformation towards the destination is refined into a series\nof bounded transitions under §4 Refinement, each carried out by its own\nstep; work that fits one activation is a single transition. Each\ntransition binds the obligations it must preserve: the outer obligations\nof the destination and of the governing relations it affects, as far as\nthey apply to it.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step%2FTransitions","start_line":133}],
      "key": "transition",
      "label": "Bounded transition"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Corpus-owned construction relation binding A and Z, choosing work, composing steps, correcting discrepancies and claiming completion. Consumers apply this single relation; domain strategy, actor configuration, execution mechanisms and additional assurance retain their respective owners.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":207,"quote":"This subsection states the construction relation for this corpus: how a\nselected construction binds its current state and destination, chooses\nits work, composes its steps, corrects itself and claims completion. It\nis law carried from the common construction requirement and the universal\nconstruction model of the Product that owns this corpus, restated here at\nits owner. ACTIVATION §2 to §7, EVALUATION §1, SPEC_METHOD §4 and §8,\nEXECUTIVE_BASELINE, ODD and the other consumers named in the design\napply it; none restates it (P6).","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step%2FConstruction%20relation","start_line":200}],
      "key": "construction_relation",
      "label": "Construction relation"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Three distinct subject accounts: specification is the internal reference model of required conditions; observations describe what holds; causal or predictive models explain how action may change state. These are distinct from FOUNDATIONS' accounts of a construction.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":237,"quote":"Three accounts of the subject, distinct from the accounts of a\nconstruction ([FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#accounts-of-a-construction)).\nThe specification is the internal reference model of the required\nconditions. Observations describe what does hold. A causal or\npredictive model explains how an action may change the state. These\naccounts have different purposes and can be incomplete or wrong in\ndifferent ways; a claim about one is never taken for a claim about\nanother, and the applicability and adequacy of a predictive model are\nclaims of their own (P1).","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step%2FConstruction%20relation","start_line":229}],
      "key": "subject_accounts",
      "label": "Specification, observation and predictive accounts"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Arrangement of admissible construction and assurance serving Z within a selected resource envelope. A composition boundary is where a step's output becomes the next step's starting state; it is distinct from a categorical join, a map between categories.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":240,"quote":"A strategy arranges admissible construction and assurance to\nserve Z within the selected resource envelope.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step%2FConstruction%20relation","start_line":239},{"end_line":264,"quote":"Composition boundaries. A composition boundary is the boundary between\nsuccessive steps, where one step's output becomes the next step's\nstarting state. It is distinct from a categorical join, which is a map\nbetween categories ([FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra)).","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step%2FConstruction%20relation","start_line":261}],
      "key": "construction_strategy",
      "label": "Strategy and composition boundaries"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Feedback observes, compares governing conditions, diagnoses material discrepancy, selects an authorised response, acts and observes again. Homeostasis is correction towards required conditions without a convergence or adequacy guarantee. Bugs are observed or suspected discrepancies within feature/change work and its existing intake and delivery mechanism. Diagnosis distinguishes defective realisation, inadequate requirement or design, inaccurate predictive model and insufficient observation; severity describes consequence while priority orders response.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":289,"quote":"Diagnosis distinguishes four causes: a defective realisation, an\ninadequate governing requirement or design, an inaccurate predictive\nmodel, and insufficient observation.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step%2FConstruction%20relation","start_line":287}],
      "key": "feedback_diagnosis",
      "label": "Feedback, diagnosis and bug work"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Exact, self-reconstructing execution intake naming the governed outcome, admitted prerequisite or experiment; subject, basis and acquirable inputs; evaluation and result algebra; affected relations and invariants; accepted transformation admissions; computational dispositions; construction and assessment authorities and grant; actor envelopes; invalidation and re-entry conditions; and, for a cost claim, allowance and spend measurement.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":358,"quote":"A step is activated from an intake sufficient to reconstruct its governing\nrelations without conversation history, commentary or a prior actor's memory\n(P0, actor-change premise). The intake names:","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step%2FIntake","start_line":356}],
      "key": "intake",
      "label": "Intake"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Smallest coherent causal dependency cone capable of delivering working behaviour while preserving every affected governing relation. It need not match a function, file, module, ticket field or design document. This cone is the context procedure's seed set Z, distinct in use from construction's destination predicate Z; context is its projection.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":405,"quote":"The execution unit is the smallest coherent causal dependency cone capable\nof delivering working behaviour while preserving every affected governing\nrelation. It need not coincide with one function, file, module, ticket\nfield or design document (P0, P4b; provenance rc.2 SPEC_METHOD\n#bounded-causal-construction). A seam whose far side can causally affect,\nor be affected by, the action is inside the cone unless the basis\nestablishes that it cannot participate. Unrelated incompleteness outside\nthe cone is recorded as repricing input and does not block the bounded\nclaim. The cone is the seed set Z of §2; the context is its projection.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step%2FExecution%20unit","start_line":397}],
      "key": "execution_unit",
      "label": "Execution unit"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Step contract with at least drafted, admitted, rejected and superseded states. Drafting and admitting are separate relations even in one invocation; that distinction implies no separate turn, carrier or ceremony. An admitted contract names one durable result and evidence surface.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":413,"quote":"Drafting a step's contract and admitting it are distinct relations, even\ninside one invocation that drafts, validates, admits and executes; no\nseparate turn, carrier or approval ceremony is implied by the distinction.\nA contract carries at minimum the states drafted, admitted, rejected and\nsuperseded ([TICKETS §5](TICKETS.md#execution-contract-admission)).","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step%2FAdmission","start_line":409}],
      "key": "execution_contract",
      "label": "Execution contract and admission"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Basis-bound evaluation of the predicate that a frame obligation applies to the exact subject, owned by the evaluation and scope declarations. Exclusion is the obligation's state following falsified applicability, not a result of that obligation.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":455,"quote":"The owning evaluation and scope declarations determine which frame\nobligations apply to the exact subject. Their declared predicates are\nevaluated from sufficient basis-bound facts: a true predicate requires the\napplicable evaluation and its result; a false predicate excludes only that\nobligation, under its cited authority; a missing or ambiguous premise\nleaves applicability unresolved, not false.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step%2FApplicability","start_line":450}],
      "key": "applicability",
      "label": "Applicability and exclusion"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Candidate plus step-produced facts: judgments and evidence, residuals, observations, authority decisions, provenance and one construction-availability stop state. The actor's internal path is neither output nor governed.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":508,"quote":"The step's output is a candidate plus its step-produced facts: judgments with\ntheir evidence, residuals, observations, authority decisions, provenance, and\none stop state, a value of construction availability (§3). The actor's\ninternal path is not part of the output\nand is not governed (FOUNDATIONS §2, work boundary; provenance\n[Probabilistic Work Boundary](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#probabilistic-work-boundary)).","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step%2FOutput","start_line":503}],
      "key": "step_output",
      "label": "Step output"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Allocation of task responsibilities and information exchanges to frames across the task's work; activation binds actors to frames. The active frame configuration is the portion used for one evaluation or decision. Reconfiguration is any change of allocation during work, including actors redistributing work.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":516,"quote":"A configuration allocates a task's responsibilities and information\nexchanges to frames; activation binds an actor to each frame (§2). It\nspans the task's work. The active frame configuration of\n[FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#frame-objects) is the part of it used for\none evaluation or decision (P0, P6).","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step%2FConfiguration","start_line":512}],
      "key": "configuration",
      "label": "Configuration and reconfiguration"
    },
    {
      "conditions": ["The executive baseline profile is selected."],
      "definition": "Illustrative, nondefault configuration separating bounded change from delivery across tasks: Worker, specialised as Writer for documents and records, constructs; Reviewer assesses; Executive keeps the longer-term outcome, selects work and disposes within its grant while mutating nothing. The profile owns its frames, grants, limits, prohibitions and explanation.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":618,"quote":"Worker frame, specialised as Writer for documents and records, constructs;\na Reviewer frame assesses; an Executive frame keeps the longer-term\noutcome, selects the next work and disposes within its decision grant, and\nmutates nothing. That profile owns its frames, their grants, limits and\nprohibitions, and its explanation; they apply where it is selected. It is\nnot the method's default. A configuration with other frames, names or\ntopology is evaluated as Evaluation of a configuration above states.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step%2FConfiguration","start_line":612}],
      "key": "executive_configuration",
      "label": "Executive configuration example"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Roles are configuration-allocated relations over steps, not actor kinds or a fixed inventory. Where those operations exist, constructor owns implementation and self-review, assessor independently evaluates a frozen candidate, and decision owner disposes. Other responsibilities may be allocated.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":641,"quote":"Roles are relations over steps that a configuration allocates\n(Configuration above), not kinds of actor and not a fixed inventory.\nWhere a configuration's operations include construction, assessment or\ndisposition, this member names the responsibility for each: a\nconstructor owns the bounded implementation and its self-review; an\nassessor evaluates a frozen candidate independently; a decision owner\ndisposes. A configuration may allocate other responsibilities.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F1.%20The%20step%2FRoles%20and%20delegation","start_line":635}],
      "key": "roles_delegation",
      "label": "Roles and delegation"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Declared procedure over intake seed set Z, material dependency family R and actor envelope B: compute finite unique material closure on an exact basis; project with explicit seams; test envelope fit; acquire declared inputs by exact identity. Here seed Z comprises subject, outcome and affected relations, not the destination predicate's use of Z.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":713,"quote":"Given a seed set Z (the subject, outcome and affected relations named in the\nintake), a relation family R (the dependency relations whose change can\nalter the result, basis validity, evidence sufficiency or authority), and\nthe actor's envelope B:","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F2.%20Context%20construction%20under%20an%20envelope","start_line":710}],
      "key": "context_construction",
      "label": "Context construction under an envelope"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Acquisition is read-only observation of the frame, subject and declared inputs permitted by intake, not admission or an additional actor stage. A derived surface copies, projects or compresses owning sources, names them and owns no determination; a current a_c task constraint surface is one such surface.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":806,"quote":"Acquisition. Acquisition is the read-only observation of the material a\nstep needs (its frame, its subject and its declared inputs) within the\ninputs its intake permits it to acquire (§1 Intake). It is not an admission and not a further\nactor stage; effectful work still needs its admitted contract (§1\nAdmission), and acquiring material grants no role, operation or decision\n([FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What\ncreates no authority). A derived surface is material derived from owning\nsources by copying, projection or compression, such as a projected frame\nfor a task; it names its sources and owns no determination. Where a\ncurrent interpretation of the subject in `a_c` exists, the constraint\nsurface it yields for the task is such a derived surface, under the\nconditions of\n[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §9 Constraint surfaces](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#constraint-surfaces).","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F2.%20Context%20construction%20under%20an%20envelope","start_line":794}],
      "key": "acquisition_derived_surface",
      "label": "Acquisition and derived surfaces"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Prompt is rendered contract over typed authority, not source law. It projects current authority references, obligations, contracts, boundaries, proof expectations and fallback conditions needed by the step.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":867,"quote":"Prompt construction. A prompt is rendered contract over typed authority;\nit is not source law. Prompt text must project the current authority\nreferences, obligations, contracts, boundaries, proof expectations and\nfallback conditions the step needs.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F2.%20Context%20construction%20under%20an%20envelope","start_line":864}],
      "key": "prompt_contract",
      "label": "Prompt construction"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Source-identity currentness of a derived surface for a selected basis, applicable to any method and carrier. Currentness, fidelity, question-specific sufficiency and source ownership are separate matters.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":907,"quote":"This subsection owns when a derived surface (Acquisition above) is current\nand when it is stale, for any method and any carrier (P3, P5, P6):","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F2.%20Context%20construction%20under%20an%20envelope%2FStaleness%20of%20derived%20surfaces","start_line":906}],
      "key": "surface_currentness",
      "label": "Staleness of derived surfaces"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Five result refinements with distinct questions and mapping predicates: admission/activation—lawfully admitted and activated on exact subject and basis; construction availability—a candidate is available; disposition—candidate accepted at declared boundary; ambiguity outcome—declared ambiguity resolved on exact basis; effects—intended effect occurred.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":967,"quote":"| admission and activation | may the step begin | the step is lawfully admitted and activated on the exact subject and basis |\n| construction availability | did the step yield its output | a candidate is available |\n| disposition | what the decision owner does with an assessed candidate | the candidate is accepted at its declared boundary |\n| ambiguity outcome | what happened to a declared ambiguity | the declared ambiguity is resolved on the exact basis |\n| effects | did an intended external effect occur | the intended effect occurred |","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F3.%20Step%20results%20and%20disposition","start_line":963}],
      "key": "result_refinements",
      "label": "Core result refinements"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "Pre-step result domain for lawful admission and activation on exact subject and basis. Values named here are activated, admission_refused(authority), admission_refused(basis), closure_unresolved, out_of_frame and activation_refusal with its cause. REFERENCE_FRAME owns the frame activate refinement and its causes and core mappings.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":985,"quote":"A step exists only after its contract is admitted (§1, Admission) and its\nframe is activated on the exact subject and basis (§2). The outcomes of\nadmission and of context construction are owned here; each maps for the\npredicate \"the step is lawfully admitted and activated on the exact\nsubject and basis\", and its cause selects its value (P5, P6; RF-005 for\nthe basis causes). The outcomes of frame activation are the `activate`\nrefinement of [REFERENCE_FRAME §5](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#5-method-functions),\nwhich owns their causes, their predicate and their core values. Because\nthis predicate requires activation, a refused activation decides it with\nthe value REFERENCE_FRAME §5 gives; the table names those outcomes and\nmaps none of them again:","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F3.%20Step%20results%20and%20disposition%2FAdmission%20and%20activation","start_line":975}],
      "key": "admission_activation_result",
      "label": "Admission and activation outcomes"
    },
    {
      "conditions": ["Lawful activation has occurred."],
      "definition": "Result domain deciding whether the step's output exists. Output remains a candidate until evaluated: the constructed subject for a constructing step or closed results for an assessing step. Values are candidate_ready, refused, incomplete, re_entry_requested(authority) and re_entry_requested(basis).",
